analysis.title: GS FINS & REITs Daily (Nov 13, 2026)
key_insights: Pre-market US futures are up slightly (SPX +25bps, NDX +15bps, RTY +25bps). The global MSFT 365 outage has MSFT -1.5% pre-market. NVDA +2% pre-market. AMAT +60bps, CBRS +17% and CSCO -2.75% after earnings.

Today's focus is the 8:30am US PPI release and a run of Fed speakers: Goolsbee, Collins (twice), Logan, Bowman, Daly and Jefferson. Next week: Warsh speaks Monday 11/16, NVDA reports 11/17, retail earnings (HD 11/17, LOW/TGT 11/18, WMT 11/19), China tech earnings (Tencent 11/18, BABA 11/19), and a Trump-Xi meeting 11/18-11/19.

The S&P Financial Index closed -0.72% last session, 8.0% above its 200DMA with a 14-day RSI of 59. Only 16% of S&P Financial stocks rose. Financials single-stock volume was -25% vs the 20DMA and sector ETF volume about -35%. P&C Insurance, Large Cap Banks and Trust Banks outperformed. Payments, Alts and Consumer Finance lagged.

Rates and risk moved the wrong way last session: 2yr +14bps to 4.88%, 10yr +13bps to 5.12%, 30yr +9bps to 5.45%, VIX +7% to 19, MOVE +8% to 92, Bitcoin -4% to 71.4k, IG CDX -1% to 59, HY CDX -1% to 348.

HOOD October metrics were mixed. Net deposits rose about $9bn sequentially to about $15bn (including about $6.5bn from Trump Accounts), a 46% annualized growth rate (26% excluding Trump accounts) against 20% annual NNA guidance. About 200k new accounts took funded accounts to 28.9mn (8% annualized growth). Margin balances were $22.9bn (+4% MoM). Event contracts rose 5% MoM to 5.9bn.

HOOD negatives: crypto volumes fell 21% MoM and 48% YoY (Robinhood App -24%/-51%, Bitstamp -18%/-46%). Net securities lending revenue was negative for a third straight quarter at -$12mn. Platform assets fell 3% MoM to $383.2bn.

CHYM roadshow takeaways: Chime Prime is still in early innings and likely to drive the business into 2027. The company is focused on closing the Stride Bank acquisition. The spotlight is on the pro forma return profile.

Agentic payments: a WSJ article says AI bots are using credit cards and banks are racing to keep up. BAC, CF and C cards are being used by agents, while JPM has been blocking agents when consumers give bots their card information. Fraud and legal risk handling is a concern.
Regulatory: Trump nominated a bipartisan slate of CFTC and SEC commissioners, relevant for exchanges and traditional market structure incumbents.

Investment banks (Yaro and team) see non-M&A advisory, notably restructuring, as constructive. M&A is mid-cycle, led by strategic and large-cap deals, while sponsor and mid-cap M&A is more muted. Modest operating leverage continues. Elevated cash balances give buyback and inorganic growth optionality. Preferred names: EVR, LCLN, PIPR, PJT.

Info Services post-3Q themes: the AI debate is becoming more differentiated, macro sensitivity is producing more varied outcomes, hyperscaler capex is fueling investment grade issuance, buy-side and sell-side budgets are healthy, consumer credit is solid outside mortgage, pricing is a revenue tailwind, and event-driven activity is elevated.

STAG 4Q operating update as of Nov 6: 3.1mn sqft leased (0.9mn new, 2.2mn renewals) vs 3.6mn total in 3Q26. Cash rent change was +20% (3Q 23.8%, YTD 21%) and straight-line rent change +37.3%. Retention was 77% adjusted for immediate backfills. 42.8% of expected 2027 leasing is addressed at a 12.2% cash rent change, and the company expects FY27 cash rent change of 15%.
WY presentation: lumber 4QTD realizations are -$55/MBF vs the 3Q average, currently -$65/MBF. OSB is +$15/MSF vs the 3Q average, currently +$20.

Street actions: COLD raised to Overweight at Piper Sandler. HWC cut to Neutral at Piper (PT $71.50). ARE cut to Underperform at BofA (PT $45). NHI cut to Underperform at BofA (PT $67). BPOP reinstated Market Perform at Hovde (PT $171).

GIR Global Markets Outlook 2027 ('Growing Pains'): the macro forecast is friendly (stable growth, declining inflation, peaking policy rates), but late-cycle headwinds are building. Real rates are higher, credit spreads wider and volatility rising under the surface. The AI impulse looks poised to peak in the coming year, and the Iran war has upended many forecasts.
